Evidence indicates that Herod died in 4 BC (see Richard Neitzel Holzapfel, “King Herod,”BYU Studies, vol. 36, no. 3, [1996–97], 55, 63, 68). The dating system of BC (“before Christ”) and AD (Anno Domini, Latin for “in the year of the Lord”) was established by a Christian monk in the sixth century AD. Herod’s death date challenges this dating system because, according to Matthew, Herod was king when Jesus was born in Bethlehem (seeMatthew 2:1). We also learn from Matthew that the Wise Men later found Jesus in Bethlehem as a young child. Soon after their visit, Herod ordered the death of all children ages two years old and younger in Bethlehem. If Herod’s death date is accurate, this suggests that Jesus was born prior to 4 BC. There is disagreement among scholars as to the precise date of the Savior’s birth (see Lincoln H. Blumell and Thomas A. Wayment, “When Was Jesus Born: A Response to a Recent Proposal,”BYU Studies, vol. 51, no. 3 [2012], 53–81).
